channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: One dead, four injured in Paris-area shooting; police probe racist or religious motive
item.description: One person was killed and four others, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded after a man opened fire in Trappes and La Verrière, west of Paris, on Friday morning.

item.title: Ukraine still reports issues with Starshield, despite Trump announcing restoration of access
item.description: Ukraine’s military still faces restrictions on SpaceX’s Starshield satellite communications system.

item.title: Hot summer claimed the lives of more than 50,000 Europeans
item.description: The extreme heat last summer has claimed the lives of more than 50,000 people in Europe, according to a new study.

item.title: PHP Warns: Outdated websites remain vulnerable to attacks
item.description: Websites running on outdated versions of PHP remain vulnerable unless they are updated, the PHP Foundation has warned.

item.title: ‘I stayed in emergency mode’: How Iranian students in Belgium grapple with the ongoing war
item.description: While internet access in Iran has been partially restored and the protests have been crushed, the crisis hasn’t ended for Iranian students in Belgium.

item.title: France to deploy military in support of police ahead of fresh protests
item.description: France will tighten security on Saturday, deploying soldiers to support police ahead of fresh protests, while all demonstrations have been banned in Lyon.

item.title: ‘Overshoot is not surrender’: UN issues strong warnings ahead of climate change summit
item.description: “Every additional fraction of a degree and additional year of warming above 1.5°C increases climate impacts and risks."

item.title: Belgian Foreign Minister condemns alliance between former Congo leader and M23 rebels
item.description: Maxime Prévot has condemned the alliance between the former President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Joseph Kabila, and the M23 rebel movement.

item.title: PM De Wever 'certain' European Commission will not reopen debate on Russian assets
item.description: Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever (NV-A) said he is certain the European Commission will not reopen the debate over using frozen Russian assets held at Euroclear to help finance Ukraine.

item.title: US Ambassador White denies intelligence delays as report links Musk to Ukraine network restrictions
item.description: US Ambassador to Belgium Bill White has denied that Washington is deliberately withholding or delaying intelligence on Russian attacks in Ukraine.

item.title: What countries have issued travel warnings over Europe's civil unrest?
item.description: As of Tuesday, 17 countries have issued travel warnings to citizens living in or visiting France, Belgium and Italy.

item.title: 'Avoid large crowds': Belgian government warns countrymen in France
item.description: The Belgian Ministry of Foreign Affairs has issued a warning to Belgians in France to avoid large crowds and meetings following the riots in the country on Saturday.

item.title: 'A louse in a house': How a mysterious cyber incident paralysed a Dutch supermarket chain
item.description: The biggest disruptions happened in the Netherlands, but Albert Heijn and Delhaize shops in Belgium also faced supply problems and shortages.

item.title: Thailand joins countries warning against travel to Belgium amid protests
item.description: The warning was issued following a series of violent demonstrations across Europe this past weekend.

item.title: Pope addresses crowd for first time since lung surgery
item.description: The head of 1.4 billion Catholics returned to public view a day after discharge, thanking supporters for their prayers after surgery to remove a cancerous nodule from his right lung.

item.title: Lithuania accuses Moscow of sabotage attacks
item.description: Flammable liquids were found at a secret satellite site after a 2:00 attempted arson attack, in what Lithuania says fits a wider pattern of sabotage seen across Europe.

item.title: China to heavily restrict AI export
item.description: China has proposed tighter export controls on 40 technologies, with 14 facing outright bans and 26 requiring official approval before transfer abroad.

item.title: Four European countries sign free trade agreement with Vietnam
item.description: The agreement covers trade in goods and services, intellectual property rights, trade defence measures and sustainable development.

item.title: European Council leaves Ukraine in uncertainty about delivery of anti-ballistic interceptors
item.description: “We’ll keep on living – living with dignity – and fighting.”

item.title: Pope Leo XIV fit to be discharged from hospital
item.description: The Pope had surgery to remove a cancerous lung nodule. He will leave the hospital in the early afternoon.
